context_requirements: Expression of COX-1 and/or COX-2 (PTGS1/PTGS2) for on-target enzyme inhibition
Active prostaglandin synthesis and autocrine/paracrine prostaglandin signaling
Intact inflammatory or stress-responsive signaling (NF-kB, AP-1) for early gene modulation
Proliferative drive and/or apoptosis sensitivity for late antiproliferative effects
falsifiers: No change in PTGS2 or other immediate-early inflammatory genes at 6 h in any line
No antiproliferative or apoptotic signature at 24 h in lines with high COX expression
Strong and consistent transcriptional response in COX-null lines
Lack of any dose- or time-dependent gene expression changes at 10 micromolar

evidence.supports: Sulindac sulfide at 10 micromolar alters expression of 65 genes in colorectal cancer cells, with time- and dose-dependent changes and apoptosis induction
Piroxicam reduces tumor volume and induces apoptosis in a canine bladder cancer model
Piroxicam plus cisplatin increases apoptotic index and reduces angiogenesis in canine bladder cancer
COX-2 inhibition reduces UVB-induced inflammation and PGE2 levels in skin
H2S-releasing COX inhibitor accelerates recovery from spinal cord injury, indicating anti-inflammatory effects

changes: Removed PTGS2 from proximal_up: COX inhibition does not transcriptionally induce PTGS2; PTGS2 was also listed in proximal_down, and a gene must not appear in both lists.
Removed PTGS2 from proximal_down: direct COX enzyme inhibition is not expected to lower PTGS2 transcription at 6 h; PTGS2 is the drug target, not a proximal transcriptional readout.

Kept immediate-early inflammatory genes (EGR1, FOS, JUN, ATF1, NFKBIA/B/E, IER3, ZFP36, DUSP4/6, CXCL2, IL1B, TRIB1) in proximal_up as stress/AP-1/NF-kB feedback responses, but confidence remains low because the cited abstracts do not establish these specific directions.
Kept late antiproliferative/pro-apoptotic genes in late_up and late_down as generic downstream consequences, but these are not proximal COX targets.

Evidence retained: all five cited abstracts support the general anti-inflammatory, antiangiogenic, or pro-apoptotic effects of COX inhibitors; none directly validates the specific landmark gene directions listed.
